name: Afghanistan
fact: Afghanistan's first national park, Band-e Amir, features six striking deep-blue lakes created by natural mineral dams across the rugged Hindu Kush.

name: Armenia
fact: Armenia made chess a mandatory subject in primary schools nationwide, fostering strategic thinking and problem-solving skills in young minds.

name: Azerbaijan
fact: More than four hundred bubbling mud volcanoes dot the landscape of Azerbaijan, representing over half of the world's total mud volcano formations.

name: Bahrain
fact: The Bahrain World Trade Center was the first skyscraper in the world to integrate large-scale wind turbines directly into its architectural design.

name: Bangladesh
fact: Spanning the southern coast of Bangladesh, the Sundarbans forms the largest contiguous mangrove forest on Earth and shelters diverse wildlife.

name: Bhutan
fact: By absorbing significantly more carbon dioxide than it emits, Bhutan stands proudly as one of the world's few carbon-negative nations.

name: Brunei
fact: Ulu Temburong National Park preserves vast tracts of pristine primary rainforest, accessible mainly by traditional longboats to protect delicate biodiversity.

name: Cambodia
fact: Angkor Wat stands as the largest religious monument on Earth, celebrated for its intricate sandstone bas-reliefs and visionary ancient Khmer engineering.

name: China
fact: Decades of dedicated reforestation and habitat protection across China successfully lifted the iconic giant panda off the endangered species list.

name: Cyprus
fact: Protected coastal beaches across Cyprus serve as vital nesting sanctuaries for endangered green and loggerhead sea turtles returning annually to the Mediterranean.

name: Georgia
fact: Winemakers in Georgia continue an unbroken eight-thousand-year tradition of fermenting vintage grapes inside large subterranean clay vessels known as qvevri.

name: India
fact: With the triumphant Chandrayaan-3 mission, India achieved the historic scientific milestone of soft-landing an exploration rover near the Moon's south pole.

name: Indonesia
fact: The coral reefs of Raja Ampat harbor the richest marine biodiversity documented anywhere on Earth, sheltering over five hundred species of coral.

name: Iran
fact: Ancient Persian engineers developed the ingenious qanat system, utilizing subterranean aqueducts to channel fresh mountain water across arid plains for sustainable agriculture.

name: Iraq
fact: Extensive ecological restoration revived the Mesopotamian Marshes, returning lush wetlands and migrating waterfowl to this UNESCO-protected cradle of ancient civilization.

name: Israel
fact: Pioneering drip irrigation and advanced wastewater recycling, Israeli agricultural engineers enabled thriving crop yields in arid desert environments worldwide.

name: Japan
fact: Operating at high speeds since 1964, the iconic Shinkansen rail network has maintained a flawless passenger safety record throughout six decades of service.
